class_id: a config key written in a different naming form than the callers use, so its rules silently never apply
feature: the field priority matrix (scraper/src/config/field-priority-matrix.ts) and any other per-field config table looked up by a field name that callers spell in another form (snake_case vs camelCase, table column vs ORM property)
symptom: the lookup normalises the caller's name (toCamelKey) and falls back to the raw string. An entry keyed in the OTHER form is reachable only by a caller that passes that form -- in practice, only a test. Production callers pass the real property name, miss the entry, and get the DEFAULT rules, with no error and no log. A test written with the entry's own spelling passes, so it pins the dead entry and hides the miss. Wider shape: any second key space (alias, CLI name, snake/camel) that is not validated against the real set of names turns configuration into dead text.
